text:
## Headline

**Platform held 99.94% uptime in Q3 against a 99.9% SLO**, with P95 latency down 12.3% to 184ms and MTTR cut from 51 minutes to 42. Incident volume dropped 22%, and we held zero Sev 1s in the last four weeks of the quarter.

## What moved

Weekly uptime improved monotonically from 99.85% in W27 to a peak of 99.97% in W38, with the only dip in W39 from a controlled maintenance window. **P95 latency fell from 212ms to 184ms**. Most of the improvement came from the caching layer rollout that landed in W31-W32.

MTTR is the headline operational metric: dropped from 51 min to 42 min, a **17.6% reduction**. Driver was the new on-call runbook adoption + the auto-rollback flag we shipped in W29. **Incidents (Sev 1-2) fell from 9 in Q2 to 7 in Q3**, with severity mix improving. Only 2 Sev 1s in the quarter vs 4 in Q2.

## So what

The platform exceeded its SLO by a healthy margin while shipping at the same release cadence as Q2. The reliability lift came from process changes (runbooks, auto-rollback) more than from a feature freeze. Capacity utilization at **68.4%** gives us roughly 18 months of headroom at current growth before the next scaling threshold. Recommend pulling the Q4 capacity planning forward by one sprint to maintain the buffer.

## Talking points

- **Zero Sev 1s in the last 4 weeks**. a real cultural signal. The auto-rollback flag (shipped W29) caught two would-be incidents before they reached customer impact
- **MTTR -17.6% is the under-told win**. Process change, not tooling. On-call runbook adoption hit 92% by end of quarter
- **Auth + Payments incidents (5 of 7)** dominate the service breakdown. Both are scoped for the Q4 reliability sprint. The architecture-review docs are already in flight
- **Caching layer rollout (W31-W32) drove the P95 latency drop**. Single highest-leverage shipped change of the quarter
- **Capacity at 68.4%** sits inside the 60-75% sweet-spot band. No immediate scaling work, but plan-ahead for Q1

## Risks + caveats

The 99.97% peak in W38 is hard to sustain quarter over quarter. Set Q4 expectations at 99.93%+ rather than "better than last quarter" to avoid setting a treadmill. Auth service had **3 of 7 Sev 2 incidents**. Single-point concentration. The W36 Redis-drift incident in NAMER suggests we should accelerate the multi region replica work, which currently is queued for Q1. Notifications service incident (W37, SES quota exhaustion) traced to a missing alarm. The alarm-coverage audit was already on the Q4 reliability sprint but is now Priority 1 given the cause.
